notes: DISCOVERED during the construction-spending-2026-11-02 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Two measured reasons it belongs on the calendar. First, housing starts is one of the EIGHT TRIGGER releases in the Atlanta Fed workbook — the same column as construction spending, ISM Manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail sales + inventories, international trade (full report), advance Census manufacturing (M3-1) and personal income and outlays — so it causes a posted GDPNow vintage in its own right, unlike the ten 'other releases' folded in opportunistically. Second, it reads the SAME September 2026 reference month as the proposing print, from the residential-supply side; residential construction is 40.4% of the proposing print's aggregate ($871.2B of $2,157.6B SAAR, FRED TLRESCONS/TTLCONS through July 2026) and its fastest-falling component (-7.3% y/y, -11.7% below its May-2022 peak). The series is almost entirely untracked: housing-starts-2026-12-17 is canonical and housing-starts-2026-11-18 exists only as a proposal, while the October edition — the last trigger vintage before the 2026:Q4 nowcast opens on 2026-10-29 — has no entry of any kind. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same measured grounds as the sibling Census entries: no macro-keyed house playbook (re-grepped 2026-09-06, 0 hits), no instrument attaches. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
